# LinkShell

> LinkShell lets you follow, steer and approve the coding agents running on your computer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor CLI, and ACP agents) from an iPhone, Android phone, or Apple Watch, with a 120fps WebRTC/Metal remote desktop control of a Mac (1080p60 DXGI H.264 on Windows), a terminal, and local web previews. Between two Macs, Fusion Mode opens another Mac's apps as local windows. Traffic between phone and computer is end-to-end encrypted (`Ed25519` + `X25519` + `XChaCha20-Poly1305`); the relay gateway is open source (MIT) and can be self-hosted free.

## How it works

- **Host** (`linkshell host`): daemon on macOS, Windows 10/11, WSL2, or Linux that owns agent sessions, PTY terminals, localhost port previews, and the desktop screen stream.
- **Clients**: native iOS + watchOS app, Android APK, standalone macOS/Windows desktop workspace, and E2E-encrypted web console.
- **Encryption & Gateway**: peers authenticate via `Ed25519` signatures and establish ephemeral `X25519` + `XChaCha20-Poly1305` E2E tunnels. The gateway sees only ciphertext. Self-host `nickname4th/linkshell-gateway` free (MIT), or sign in with LinkShell Pro to use the managed global gateway + TURN screen relay.
- **Fusion Mode (Mac to Mac)**: renders apps from a remote Mac in your local Dock & Cmd+Tab with virtual per-app WebRTC displays and shared clipboard.

## Install

- Desktop app (macOS Silicon/Intel notarized DMG & Windows x64): https://github.com/LiuTianjie/LinkShell/releases/latest
- CLI: `npm i -g linkshell-cli`, `brew install LiuTianjie/linkshell/linkshell`, or `curl -fsSL https://liutianjie.github.io/LinkShell/install.sh | sh`
- One-time setup: `linkshell setup`
